metadata.title: A Teachers’ Guide to TALIS 2013: Teaching and Learning International Survey

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS 2013 teachers’ guide describes a large-scale survey of lower secondary teachers and school leaders, with teachers and leaders randomly selected within schools (20 teachers and 1 school leader per school). The document reports descriptive percentages and averages across participating countries/economies and notes that results are based on the TALIS 2013 database, implying the use of TALIS sampling design features when producing country estimates. However, the guide does not specify the exact sampling weight variable names (e.g., student/teacher weights) or any replicate-weight scheme, so the precise weighting and variance-estimation approach cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For analysts using TALIS microdata, complex survey weights should be applied to obtain population-representative estimates and to account for clustering at the school level; replicate weights should be used if the TALIS database provides them for standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive teachers’ guide to TALIS 2013 and does not report any PV-based cognitive achievement modeling; TALIS in this guide focuses on teachers’ and school leaders’ working conditions, beliefs, practices, and reported perceptions rather than PV-scored achievement outcomes. Because no PV generation/combining procedure is described, plausible values handling is not applicable. The text also does not document any missing-data strategy (e.g., imputation or deletion rules), so missing-data handling is treated as a reporting gap for this specific guide excerpt.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The guide states that TALIS 2013 surveyed lower secondary teachers and school leaders. Within each participating country/economy, 200 schools were randomly selected, and within each school 20 teachers and 1 school leader were randomly selected. The document does not describe additional analytic filtering (e.g., grade restrictions beyond lower secondary, exclusions for missing questionnaire items, or subsampling for specific indicators) in the provided text; it presents results based on the TALIS 2013 database.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD TALIS 2013 teachers’ guide summarizes findings from the Teaching and Learning International Survey, which focuses on teachers’ working conditions and the learning environment in lower secondary schools. TALIS 2013 used a two-stage sampling approach: 200 schools per participating country/economy were randomly selected, and within each school 20 teachers and 1 school leader were randomly selected, yielding about 107,000 teacher responses representing more than 4 million teachers across 30+ participating systems. The questionnaire (45–60 minutes, paper or online) covers school leadership, teacher training and professional development, appraisal and feedback, pedagogical beliefs and teaching practices, and teachers’ self-efficacy and job satisfaction. The guide reports descriptive cross-country patterns (e.g., shares of teachers participating in professional development, time spent on teaching/planning/marking, and relationships between classroom composition and self-efficacy/job satisfaction) rather than estimating predictive ML models. As a result, no PV handling, missing-data strategy, or ML performance metrics are provided in this excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive OECD guide rather than an empirical ML paper: it does not specify a predictive target variable, does not train or evaluate ML algorithms, and does not report model performance metrics. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and main findings are intentionally empty. The document also does not provide technical details on PV generation/combining or missing-data handling, because the reported outcomes are questionnaire-based indicators and descriptive relationships rather than PV-scored achievement modeling.
